content:
Ten years ago, a Hyderabad founder made a hiring decision most companies might have overlooked.

He hired a Class 9-pass taxi driver with no corporate experience and limited English.

What he saw wasn’t a perfect resume.
He saw reliability, willingness to learn, and potential.

Instead of asking, “Does this person have all the skills?” the company asked, “Can we help this person grow?”

He received spoken-English training, mentorship, new responsibilities, and opportunities to prove himself.

A decade later, that same employee reportedly heads the company’s procurement function.

This is more than a hiring story.

It’s a reminder that talent doesn’t always arrive fully prepared.

Sometimes, the best employees are discovered when leaders look beyond degrees, language, and impressive resumes.

Hiring for potential requires patience.

Developing people requires investment.

And giving someone their first real opportunity can change the entire direction of their career.

Good leaders don’t just find talent.

They create the environment where talent can grow.🚀
